translation_en: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The right of pre-emption applies to shared land, a house, or a garden. A partner should not sell until he offers it to his partner, who may take it or leave it; if the partner declines, he has the greater right until notified.”

Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “None of you should prevent his neighbor from placing a wooden beam in his wall.” Abu Hurairah then said, “Why do I see you turning away from this? By Allah, I will cast it between your shoulders!”

This report comes through another chain, with wording similar to the preceding narration and the same chain of transmission. The transmission includes Zuhayr ibn Harb, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, Abu al-Tahir, Harmalah ibn Yahya, Ibn Wahb, Yunus, Abd ibn Humayd, Abd al-Razzaq, and Maamar, all reporting it from al-Zuhri.

Sa‘id ibn Zayd reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Whoever wrongfully takes a handspan of land, Allah will encircle him with it from seven earths on the Day of Resurrection.” Its transmitters include Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Said, Ali ibn Hujr, Ismail ibn Jafar, al-Ala ibn Abd al-Rahman, Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sad, and Said ibn Zayd.

Sa‘id ibn Zayd said that Arwa disputed with him over part of his house. He said he had heard the Messenger of Allah say: “Whoever takes a handspan of land without right will be encircled by it from seven earths on the Day of Resurrection.” He prayed that, if she was lying, Allah would blind her and make her grave in her house. The narrator saw her blind, feeling along the walls and saying that Sa‘id’s supplication had afflicted her. She later fell into a well in the house, which became her grave.

‘Urwah reported that Arwa bint Uways accused Sa‘id ibn Zayd of taking her land and brought the dispute before Marwan ibn al-Hakam. Sa‘id said he would not take anything after hearing the Messenger of Allah say: “Whoever wrongfully takes a handspan of land will be encircled by it as far as seven earths.” Marwan said he would ask for no further proof. Sa‘id prayed that if she were lying, she be blinded and die on her land. She lost her sight and later fell into a pit there and died. The chain is Hammad ibn Zayd, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, Urwah.
Sa‘id ibn Zayd said: “I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: ‘Whoever wrongfully takes a handspan of land will be encircled by it from seven earths on the Day of Resurrection.’”

Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “No one may take a handspan of land without right, for Allah will encircle him with it from seven earths on the Day of Resurrection.”

Abu Salamah said he had a dispute with his people over land and went to ‘Aishah. She said, “Avoid taking the land, for the Messenger of Allah said: ‘Whoever wrongfully takes even a handspan of land will be encircled by it from seven earths.’” The chain includes Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi, Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith, Harb ibn Shaddad, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, and Muhammad ibn Ibrahim.

This report comes through another chain. It says Abu Salamah went to ‘Aishah and mentioned the matter, as in the preceding narration. Its chain is Ishaq ibn Mansur, Habban ibn Hilal, Aban, Yahya, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, and Abu Salamah.

Abu Hurairah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “When you disagree about a road, its width is set at seven cubits.” The chain is Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn al-Jahdari, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar, Khalid al-Hadhdha, Yusuf ibn Abdullah, his father, and Abu Hurairah.

Usamah ibn Zayd reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, and a disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim.” The transmitters are Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Ibn Uyaynah, al-Zuhri, Ali ibn Husayn, Amr ibn Uthman, and Usamah ibn Zayd.
Ibn ‘Abbas reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “Give the prescribed inheritance shares to those entitled to them; whatever remains goes to the nearest male relative.”

Ibn ‘Abbas reported from the Messenger of Allah: “Give the prescribed shares to those entitled to them; whatever remains after those shares goes to the nearest male relative.” Its chain is Umayyah ibn Bistam, Yazid ibn Zuray, Rawh ibn al-Qasim, Abd Allah ibn Tawus, and his father, Tawus.

Ibn ‘Abbas reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “Divide the estate among those entitled to prescribed shares according to the Book of Allah. Whatever remains goes to the nearest male relative.” The transmitters include Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn Rafi, Abd ibn Humayd, Abd al-Razzaq, Maamar, Ibn Tawus, his father, and Ibn Abbas.

This report comes through another chain, with wording similar to the narrations of Wuhaib and Rawh ibn al-Qasim. The chain is Muhammad ibn al-Ala Abu Kurayb, Zayd ibn Hubab, Yahya ibn Ayyub, and Ibn Tawus, from his father.

Jabir ibn Abdullah said he fell ill and the Messenger of Allah and Abu Bakr visited him. He lost consciousness; the Prophet performed ablution and sprinkled some water over him, and he recovered. Jabir asked how to dispose of his property, but received no answer until the inheritance verse was revealed: “They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning one who has no direct heirs.” (Quran 4:176)

Jabir ibn Abdullah said the Prophet and Abu Bakr visited him while he was unconscious. The Prophet performed ablution and sprinkled water over him. Jabir recovered and asked what to do with his property; then this was revealed: “Allah instructs you concerning your children: a male shall receive a share equal to that of two females.” (Quran 4:11)

Jabir ibn Abdullah said the Messenger of Allah and Abu Bakr visited him during his illness and found him unconscious. The Messenger performed ablution and poured some water over him. Jabir recovered and asked what to do with his property, but received no answer until the inheritance verse was revealed. The chain includes Ubayd Allah ibn Umar al-Qawariri, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, Sufyan, and Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, reporting from Jabir ibn Abdullah.

Jabir ibn Abdullah said the Messenger of Allah visited him while he was ill and unable to think clearly. After the Prophet performed ablution and they poured some water over Jabir, he recovered and said, “I have no heirs except distant relatives.” Then the inheritance verse was revealed. Asked whether this meant Quran 4:176, “They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning one who has no direct heirs,” Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir replied, “That is how it was revealed.”

In this same chain, Wahb ibn Jarir’s version says the verse of prescribed shares was revealed; al-Nadr and al-‘Aqadi’s versions say the verse prescribing the shares was revealed. None of their versions includes Shu‘bah’s statement to Ibn al-Munkadir. The report also notes that these are variant wordings of the same account in the cited transmission, and that the named narrators did not include the additional remark attributed to Shubah.

‘Umar ibn al-Khattab said in a Friday sermon that no matter concerned him more than the case of one with no direct heirs. He had repeatedly asked the Messenger of Allah about it, who was especially stern with him and prodded his chest, saying, “Does the summer verse at the end of Surat al-Nisa’ not suffice for you, ‘Umar?” ‘Umar said that if he lived, he would issue a ruling anyone could follow, whether or not they read the Quran. The transmitters include Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Yahya ibn Said, Hisham, Qatadah, Salim ibn Abi al-Jad, and Maadan ibn Abi Talhah.

This report comes through another chain, with wording similar to the preceding narration. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah reported through Ismail ibn Ulayyah and Said ibn Abi Arubah. Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Rafi reported through Shababah ibn Sawwar and Shubah. Both chains report from Qatadah with similar wording.
Al-Bara’ reported: “The last verse revealed from the Quran was: ‘They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning one who has no direct heirs.’” (Quran 4:176)

Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib said: “The last verse revealed was the verse about one who has no direct heirs, and the last surah revealed was Surat Bara’ah (at-Tawbah).” The chain is Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar, from Muhammad ibn Jafar, from Shubah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara ibn Azib.

Al-Bara’ reported that the last complete surah revealed was Surat at-Tawbah and that the last verse revealed was the verse about one who has no direct heirs. The transmitters are Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali, Isa ibn Yunus, Zakariyya, Abu Ishaq, and al-Bara.
This is a similar report, except that it says: “The last surah revealed in its entirety.” The chain is Abu Kurayb, Yahya ibn Adam, Ammar ibn Rizq, Abu Ishaq, and al-Bara.
Al-Bara’ said: “The last verse revealed was ‘They ask you for a ruling.’” The transmitters are Amr al-Naqid, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, Malik ibn Mighwal, Abu al-Safar, and al-Bara.

Abu Hurairah reported that when someone who owed a debt died, the Messenger of Allah asked whether the person had left anything to repay it. If enough was left, he prayed over him; otherwise he said, “Pray over your companion.” After the conquests, he said: “I have greater claim over the believers than they have over themselves. Whoever dies owing a debt, its repayment is my responsibility; whoever leaves property, it belongs to his heirs.” The transmitters include Zuhayr ibn Harb, Abu Safwan al-Umawi, Yunus al-Ayli, Harmalah ibn Yahya, Abd Allah ibn Wahb, Yunus, Ibn Shihab, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, and Abu Hurairah.

This is the same hadith through other chains of transmission from al-Zuhri. This is the same hadith through other chains from al-Zuhri: Abd al-Malik ibn Shuayb ibn al-Layth, his father and grandfather, and Uqayl; also Zuhayr ibn Harb, Yaqoub ibn Ibrahim, Ibn Akhi Ibn Shihab, Ibn Numayr, his father, and Ibn Abi Dhib.
